MSFT.macro_thesis: TECH_OUTPERFORM regime supports multiple expansion for quality large-cap tech; self-funding capex model differentiates MSFT from rate-sensitive peers in a RATES_RISING environment; $678B contracted backlog insulates near-term revenue from macro softness
MSFT.target_exit_conditions: Tactical trim if RATES_RISING regime shows imminent multiple compression transmission; trim to discovery size if any thesis breaker trips; full reassessment if two or more breakers trip simultaneously
MSFT.thesis: MSFT is an elite quality compounder with a durable multi-layer moat across Azure cloud infrastructure, OpenAI partnership, and Copilot enterprise productivity. The core bet is on Azure winning enterprise AI workloads at scale, monetized through OpenAI revenue share and Copilot adoption, self-funded from operating cash flow with AAA balance sheet strength. Reasonable valuation at 21.2x forward P/E with $678B contracted backlog provides forward revenue visibility in a TECH_OUTPERFORM regime.
thesis_breakers: Azure quarterly revenue growth decelerates below 20% YoY for two consecutive quarters
Copilot enterprise seat adoption stalls or enterprise renewal rates decline materially
AI capex spend exceeds free cash flow generation, forcing debt financing or dividend cuts

PLTR.macro_thesis: Dollar weakness regime and US defense spending prioritization support both government contract flow and international expansion. AI infrastructure buildout as a secular theme provides commercial tailwinds. Geopolitical complexity increasing demand for data intelligence platforms across allied governments.
PLTR.target_exit_conditions: Exit if forward P/E expands above 100x without corresponding acceleration in revenue growth, if government revenue declines for two consecutive quarters, or if thesis breakers are triggered. Trim opportunistically on spikes toward prior 52W high of $207.
PLTR.thesis: Palantir is a government-AI platform with a structural moat built on deeply embedded classified data infrastructure across US defense and intelligence agencies, creating switching costs no competitor can replicate. The business is transitioning from capital-intensive infrastructure builder to high-ROIC commercial compounder, with the government base providing durable high-margin revenue that funds commercial expansion. The AIP platform represents a credible second growth vector, but the position must be sized to reflect valuation risk at 75x forward P/E rather than treated as a traditional compounder.
thesis_breakers: US defense budget cuts materially reducing government contract pipeline or existing contract renewals
Commercial AIP revenue growth decelerates below 30% YoY indicating platform adoption is stalling
A credible competitor achieves FedRAMP High or equivalent classified deployment clearance at scale

TLT.macro_thesis: Fed is at or near peak rates with eventual cut cycle expected to compress long-end yields; recession risk or hard landing scenario would trigger sharp rally in long-duration Treasuries; current commodity bid and inflation risk create near-term headwind but do not invalidate the medium-term mean reversion case
TLT.target_exit_conditions: Trim above $85 or when 10-year Treasury yield reaches 4.25–4.50%; full exit if thesis breakers materialize or position no longer serves hedge function relative to rest of portfolio
TLT.thesis: TLT is held as the conservative anchor of a barbell within the IBKR account, serving three simultaneous functions: asymmetric capital appreciation in a hard landing or risk-off event, mean reversion upside as the Fed eventually cuts and long-end yields normalize, and a current income floor while the thesis plays out. Size is intentionally modest given the broader account has significant fixed income exposure elsewhere.
thesis_breakers: 10-year Treasury yield breaks decisively above 5.25% and holds, signaling structural repricing of long-end rates
Fed pivots to renewed tightening cycle in response to re-accelerating inflation above 4% CPI
US fiscal trajectory deteriorates sharply with failed Treasury auction or sovereign credit event driving long-end yields structurally higher

TSLA.macro_thesis: Grid modernization and renewable energy intermittency create structural, policy-supported demand for utility-scale energy storage; autonomy regulation is gradually liberalizing in key markets; EV penetration curve still early in most geographies outside China.
TSLA.target_exit_conditions: Trim at $420-450 zone; full reassessment if $320-330 approached with thesis-breaker confirmation; exit if any thesis-breaker event is confirmed
TSLA.thesis: TSLA is held as a high-volatility barbell position within a speculative sleeve, with two core legs: Megapack energy storage is structurally undervalued, high-margin, and growing faster than consensus as grid modernization and renewable intermittency create durable demand independent of the auto business. Autonomy optionality via vision-based FSD carries superior unit economics versus LIDAR-dependent competitors, with robotaxi and licensing upside unpriced at current levels.
thesis_breakers: Megapack order growth decelerates materially or margins compress below 20% for two consecutive quarters
FSD regulatory approval is denied or significantly delayed in a major market (US, EU, or China)
A credible LIDAR-based competitor (Waymo, Cruise) achieves commercial scale robotaxi deployment at lower cost per mile than Tesla's vision-based system

CDNS.macro_thesis: CDNS sits at the intersection of two durable macro thematics: AI infrastructure buildout and semiconductor sovereignty. Both drive sustained design activity regardless of near-term consumer chip cycles. Higher rates pressure the multiple but do not impair the business model — recurring subscription revenue is sticky through cycles. The primary macro risk is a hard landing that causes enterprise R&D budget freezes, but even in 2020 Cadence held revenue flat, demonstrating defensive characteristics. Dollar strength is a mild headwind given international revenue mix. Overall the macro setup is cautiously constructive — rate plateau or pivot removes the multiple headwind while AI chip complexity tailwinds remain intact.
CDNS.target_exit_conditions: Exit or significantly reduce if: (1) two consecutive quarters of organic ARR growth below 8% with guidance cuts, signaling real design activity slowdown not just conservatism; (2) Synopsys acquires a transformative AI-EDA platform that shifts competitive dynamics materially; (3) China revenue restrictions expand to cover substantially all semiconductor IP licensing; (4) Forward EV/FCF re-rates above 55x on euphoria without commensurate earnings acceleration, making risk-reward unfavorable. Do not exit on multiple compression alone if recurring revenue growth and ROIC remain intact.
CDNS.thesis: Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) is a high-quality EDA and IP platform business with deep structural moats — switching costs are extraordinarily high as chip design workflows are deeply embedded in customer R&D pipelines, and ROIC consistently runs above 30%. Revenue is ~90% recurring via subscriptions, giving visibility most software businesses envy. The stock has de-rated meaningfully from peak multiples alongside broader software multiple compression and near-term hyperscaler capex uncertainty, creating a rare opportunity to own a best-in-class compounder at a relative discount. AI-driven chip complexity (custom silicon, advanced packaging, chiplets) is a secular tailwind that structurally expands Cadence's TAM — more complex chips require more EDA hours and IP licensing. The business also benefits from the Systems Design and Analysis segment growing faster than core EDA, diversifying revenue. At current levels, the market is pricing in stagnation that the underlying design activity pipeline does not support.
thesis_breakers: A sustained slowdown in semiconductor R&D spending, particularly if hyperscalers pull back custom silicon programs or fabless customers cut design starts materially
Loss of competitive position to Synopsys or emerging players in AI-assisted EDA, or a successful challenge to the Cadence-Synopsys duopoly that compresses pricing power
Regulatory or geopolitical escalation that meaningfully restricts Cadence from serving Chinese customers, which represent a non-trivial revenue contribution
Multiple re-compression continuing into a higher-for-longer rate environment that keeps growth software valuations suppressed even as fundamentals hold
Execution stumbles in the Systems Analysis segment (Clarity, Celsius, Optimality) that prevent diversification away from traditional EDA and disappoint growth expectations

SMFG.macro_thesis: Japan is undergoing its most significant monetary regime shift in 30 years. The BOJ's gradual rate normalization is a structural tailwind for Japanese bank earnings that is still early innings. Inflation in Japan, while moderate, appears sticky enough to keep the BOJ on a tightening path. Global investors remain underweight Japanese financials relative to historical norms, and domestic institutional flows are rotating into value and dividend-paying equities under the Tokyo Stock Exchange's push for improved capital efficiency and ROE. A weaker yen environment has also boosted overseas earnings in yen terms. Meanwhile, global rate curves remaining elevated support SMFG's wholesale and treasury operations. The macro setup — reflation, rate normalization, governance reform pressure, and underweight positioning — is unusually aligned for a megabank re-rating.
SMFG.target_exit_conditions: Exit if BOJ pivots back to easing and forward NIM guidance deteriorates materially. Also exit if price-to-book re-rates above 1.3x without corresponding earnings growth, signaling sentiment overshoot rather than fundamental improvement. Trim on significant yen appreciation beyond 130 USD/JPY that structurally impairs the USD return thesis. Full exit if dividend growth stalls or buybacks are suspended indicating capital stress. Thesis is based on gradual re-rating and income compounding — not a momentum trade.
SMFG.thesis: SMFG (Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group) is a structurally sound Japanese megabank benefiting from the Bank of Japan's historic policy normalization after decades of zero or negative interest rates. With ROIC improving materially as net interest margins expand, SMFG trades at roughly 0.8-1.0x book value — a discount to Western peers despite a cleaner balance sheet, rising dividends, and an aggressive share buyback program. The market has partially re-rated Japanese financials but sentiment remains cautious due to yen volatility and China exposure fears, creating a quality-at-discount entry for patient capital. Structural tailwinds include domestic loan repricing, growing wealth management revenue, and a strategic push into Asian emerging markets through subsidiaries like SMBC. The 1Y return has lagged broader global financials on yen-hedging friction and macro uncertainty — exactly the dislocation this framework targets.
thesis_breakers: Bank of Japan reverses course and returns to ultra-loose policy, collapsing net interest margin expansion and the core earnings re-rating thesis
Severe credit deterioration in Japan's SME or real estate loan book driven by rate shock to over-leveraged domestic borrowers
Yen appreciates sharply and rapidly, compressing overseas earnings when translated back and reducing the USD-denominated return profile for foreign investors
Material contagion from a China financial stress event impacting SMBC's Asian loan book and cross-border exposure meaningfully
Governance regression or significant capital allocation failure such as a large dilutive acquisition at a poor price that destroys book value per share trajectory
